correctness.rationale: The proof derives actual facet areas and a two-chamber Cauchy projected-area formula. A sharp Cauchy–Schwarz analysis gives all maxima and equality cases; a strict endpoint argument gives all minima. Both thresholds, the plateau and the equal-area 3-design corollary follow algebraically. Independently projected 24-vertex hulls passed 3344 tests; these do not substitute for the analytic proof.

The full spherical-design paper proves general existence and estimates, and the full random-silhouette paper counts combinatorial shadow vertices rather than projected area. value.rationale: Gives a full and sharp endpoint/equality classification of a continuous, canonical 14-facet family. The exact flat interval sqrt(3/2) between two distinct sharp transition parameters is a structural and geometrically motivated phenomenon, and the unique equal-area spherical 3-design member lies inside. This is more than a new numeric value or routine rescaling of the published regular-member case.
